summary: Steve Eisman's weekly wrap for week ending 15 May 2026: market up sharply and feeling frothy, with narrow leadership and retail call buying; PPI jump and 10y near 4.5% raise inflation risk; private credit stress (FSK credit line cut). He lightened high flyers.

coverage.note: Premium plug and masterclass trailer; private credit lending since 2008
Masterclass end; market froth signals (semis weight, defensive share, retail calls); war, PPI, 10y yield
FSK / private credit stress, MSCI markdowns; sponsor; payment companies
Earnings recaps (Block, Bill, Trade Desk, CoreWeave, Constellation)
Cisco, mailbag on FICO and Meritage; outro

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: We have not had a credit cycle since the Great Financial Crisis. Almost all the growth in lending since 2008 has been in private credit behind a veil of privacy, which means secrecy.
claims.claim: Lending growth since 2008 sits in opaque private credit, so a new credit cycle is only now beginning and losses are hidden until marks are forced.
claims.testable: partly - opacity makes data hard to get

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: There will be losses and perhaps a recession, but not a total disaster.
claims.claim: Private credit losses probably will not cause GFC-level chaos because banks are well capitalized, though losses and a recession are possible.
claims.indicator: bank capital vs private credit losses

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: The semiconductor sector is now over 18% of the S&P. It was 14% at the start of 2026.
claims.claim: Rising semiconductor weight in the S&P is a froth signal showing concentration after a rapid rally.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: The sum of the four defensive sectors, healthcare, consumer staples, energy, and utilities represents only 19% of the S&P 500. That number was 31% at the end of 2022.
claims.claim: The shrinking weight of defensive sectors in the index (31% to 19%) signals risk appetite and concentration are high, making the market more vulnerable.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: Retail traders are buying calls in Cboe's Mag 10 stocks, which are the big seven plus AMD,
claims.claim: Aggressive retail call buying in mega-cap tech (52% of new positions calls) is a sentiment extreme resembling 2021 and a froth signal.
claims.indicator: Cboe Mag 10 retail call buying share of new positions
claims.testable: yes - options data on retail flow

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: At its bottom at the end of March, the S&P was down 4% and Nasdaq was down 7% for the year. The market is now up 9% and Nasdaq is up 15%.
claims.claim: After a sharp rebound the market partly assumes the war is over, so the rally rests on an assumption that may be wrong; the speaker lightened high flyers.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: the producer price index rose a seasonally adjusted 1.4% for the month, much higher than the 0.5% consensus forecast
claims.claim: A big producer price surprise (PPI +1.4% m/m, 6% y/y) signals inflation re-accelerating, a risk to a richly valued market.
claims.direction: inflation up, yields up, equities down
claims.testable: yes - PPI surprise is a data series

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: The 10-year yield is now flirting with 4 and 1/2%, which in the past has been a Rubicon for markets.
claims.claim: A 10-year yield around 4.5% has been a threshold above which markets in the past struggled.
claims.direction: equities down when 10y yield breaks above 4.5%

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: When a financial services company has its credit lines cut, that is always really, really bad.
claims.claim: Banks cutting a credit line to a levered lender (FSK, 650m cut, rates raised) is a stress signal of funding withdrawal in private credit.
claims.indicator: bank credit line cuts to BDCs

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: private credit funds have marked down more than 1/10 of their loans by at least 50%.
claims.claim: MSCI data show more than 10% of private credit loans marked down 50% or more, evidence of the loss cycle starting.
claims.indicator: MSCI share of private credit loans marked down 50%+

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: the problem with the space is that it's so competitive that companies are creeping into each other's businesses.
claims.claim: Payment companies outside Visa and Mastercard are poor long-term investments because competitors invade each other's verticals; Toast halved on competition and AI fears.
claims.direction: avoid payment stocks other than Visa/Mastercard

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: Block is actually up this year, 13%, but don't get too carried away here either. The stock has been in roughly this range since mid-2022.
claims.claim: Strong results after mass layoffs (Block cut over 40% of workforce, Bill up to 30%) lift earnings but the stock is range-bound, so AI-driven cost cuts do not guarantee rerating.
claims.indicator: earnings beats after AI-driven headcount cuts

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: The problem with this stock is that growth investors are leaving,
claims.claim: A fallen growth stock with decelerating growth (Trade Desk, 20% to 8%) has no marginal buyer, so it keeps falling (-46% YTD).
claims.direction: short or avoid decelerating ex-growth names

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: But when you were losing money, you can't disappoint on any metric, especially forward revenue guidance.
claims.claim: Unprofitable high-growth stocks (CoreWeave) are punished sharply for any guidance shortfall.
claims.indicator: forward revenue guidance vs consensus for unprofitable growth

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: The company had a good quarter reporting $2.74 versus $2.14 last year, which is 28% growth, and versus $2.54 expected. So, a beat. However, the stock reaction was down as management kept its $11 to $12 EPS guidance unchanged.
claims.claim: A stock can fall on an earnings beat if guidance is only maintained, because expectations already price the AI story.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: Because AI orders were very strong, the stock was up double digits on Thursday.
claims.claim: Cisco beat on EPS and revenue and guided higher on AI orders, confirming AI infrastructure demand beyond chips.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.quote: I'm bullish on Meritage long-term because buying a home builder below tangible book value, which is where the stock is now, when the
claims.claim: Buying a home builder below tangible book while it grows book value usually works out over time, but rising long-term rates force waiting.
claims.indicator: price to tangible book for homebuilders
